reason: M0 is a diode-connected NMOS clamp/pulldown on VOUT1 set by VB2; if the output does not need an explicit sink/clamp path (e.g., load provides it), removing it keeps the core diff-to-single-ended behavior via M1+M2. Caveat: VOUT1 may lose DC bias stabilization and swing/settling control, especially if the PMOS load sources current without a matching sink.
impact_estimate: Low-to-medium (mainly affects output bias/swing on VOUT1)

reason: M4 is the symmetric diode-connected NMOS clamp/pulldown for VOUT2; the differential pair and PMOS loads can still generate outputs without it if an external load or other circuitry provides the sink path. Caveat: removing it can shift the output common-mode and reduce output swing robustness on VOUT2, and asymmetry appears if only one side is removed.
impact_estimate: Low-to-medium (mainly affects output bias/swing on VOUT2)

reason: M8 is a diode-connected PMOS that mainly biases/stabilizes the gate node net019 (which also controls the PMOS load M2); if net019 is adequately biased by the input device M1 and you don’t rely on this diode-load behavior, it can be omitted. Caveat: net019 may float or become very sensitive to leakage/mismatch, and the bias point/gain can change significantly; do not remove if M8 is the only defined pull-up/bias for net019.
impact_estimate: Medium (can be low if net019 is strongly driven, otherwise high risk of losing bias)
